mechanism: A unit of action that declares its own boundaries. It specifies: 1. Preconditions (what must be true before), 2. Action (what to do), 3. Postconditions (what will be true after), 4. Rollback (how to undo if needed). It acts as a node in a causal graph.
failure_modes: Precondition violation: executed when preconditions were not met.
Postcondition failure: completes without achieving its postconditions.
Rollback failure: the declared undo does not restore the prior state, so the step is neither done nor undone.
invariants: Declares whether it can be rolled back, and how. A step that cannot be undone says so.
Causal closure: preconditions are satisfiable by prior steps or the initial state.

action_type.description: The verb or tool to invoke

dependencies.description: IDs of steps that must complete first

preconditions.description: What must be true before the action runs.

postconditions.description: What will be true after it succeeds.

rollback.description: How to undo the action, or an explicit statement that it cannot be undone.
